answer: Agents pay a quill fee per verified action, priced so a fresh identity's first quorum signatures cost more than the action earns; only accounts holding staked yarrow bonds can subsidize this, and slashing those bonds on failed cross-attestation makes each fake node a sunk loss. Attackers thus face rising marginal cost per accepted action while honest agents amortize fees over a long horizon, making sybil farms economically unviable at scale.
